as_read: Mixed: null for eczema in a primary-endpoint trial and Cochrane, some benefit in rheumatoid arthritis at high GLA doses pooled across oils, and single trials on blood pressure and weight.
stop_list: Labels print oil mass and trials mostly print GLA, so doses can't be compared without a conversion the sources don't give
Fields can't hold null for skin alongside weak positive for joint
clinician_items: 23633319: oral borage and evening primrose oil have mild, transient, mainly gastrointestinal adverse effects, and long-term use is not examined. The cited thrombosis and warfarin-bleeding reports concern evening primrose oil, not borage oil.
stored_rating_note: positive_moderate rests on one 37-patient RA trial at 1.4 g/d GLA whose authors say usual intake is far lower; the record does not reflect the null eczema trial or Cochrane, though labels carry a skin purpose.
